newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ciampi reassures Van Miert about Stet plan.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi reassures Van Miert about Stet plan.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi assured European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert on Monday that a plan to transfer telecoms firm Stet to the Treasury would go ahead despite a negative parliament vote.
"Mr Ciampi told us that it would not jeopardise the transfer of Stet to the Treasury," Van Miert told reporters after meeting Ciampi.
The lower house of the Italian parliament dealt the government an unexpected blow late on Wednesday when it voted against the transfer of Stet from state holding IRI to the Treasury.
Stet's sale is required under a 1992 agreement between the Commission and Italy to reduce IRI's huge debt in return for allowing state subsidies to IRI and its subsidiaries.

The agreement obliges IRI to cut its debt by 19 trillion lire by the end of June by selling Stet and privatising motorway operating company Autostrade, publishing company Seat and shipping firm Finmare.
"What's very important for us is that while waiting for Stet to be privatised, Stet is transferred legally to the Treasury and that the financial arrangements with IRI continue," Van Miert said.
He said Ciampi had assured him that the privatisation timetable was not in danger.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said after the parliamentary vote that the transfer arrangements can be made in other ways.
